segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Welcome to Real Easy English from BBC Learning English. I'm Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. In this podcast, we have a real conversation in easy English.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: If you want to read along, you can visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Hi Neil.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Beth. How are you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm very good, thank you. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm pretty good, yes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Good, good.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What are we talking about today?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, today we are talking about food.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: In particular, we'll talk about our favourite foods and how often we eat them.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What an amazing topic. I have so much to say about food.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: You said how often. What do we mean by how often we eat something?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Good question. How often means how many times we eat our favourite food.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So we might eat them every week, every day or if we really like a food we might eat it for breakfast, lunch and dinner, every meal.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So Neil, what is your favourite food?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, that's a really difficult question but I really like fish.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: fish Ah me too I was going to say that but actually I really love seafood So I think I say any kind of dish with seafood in it I absolutely love

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So how often do you eat seafood

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: not very often, actually. I have it when I go on holiday and I have it in restaurants sometimes,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: but I don't really cook seafood at home. What about you? How often do you have fish?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh, probably a few times a week.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Really?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Maybe, yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, we eat a lot of fish.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We sometimes have fish at home.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I normally have it once or twice a week.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But, yeah, I never have seafood at home, actually.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, OK.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So what is your least favourite food?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Oh, I absolutely hate baked beans.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You hate baked beans?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think they're disgusting.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I can't even...

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And the smell of them even makes me feel a bit sick.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh, OK.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So we've talked about the foods that we really like and the foods that we don't like.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But in a general week, what do you normally cook?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Often we'll eat Indian curries, but also Italian pasta dishes or Spanish dishes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and then sometimes more traditional British roast dinner kind of thing

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah I think generally we have the same at home like we eat a lot of food from different countries but I have to say I usually cook quite a lot of

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: pasta and quite a lot of rice at home in general just because they cook really quickly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Beth,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: you generally eat rice and pasta dishes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What does that mean, generally?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, we use generally and usually and normally

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: for habits or things that we do a lot.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, for example, if I generally cook pasta or rice,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: that means maybe five times out of the seven in a week, I would say.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, so that's most of the time.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If we use sometimes, we mean that we do it less than generally.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, sometimes might be two or three times a week.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I guess it depends on what you're talking about.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But for example, with me, I sometimes cook fish.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Like I said, I have it maybe twice a week.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So I would say that's sometimes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Beth, you said that you hate baked beans.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So do you ever eat baked beans?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Never No I can stand them So I never ever have baked beans

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well never is something that we don do We just don ever do it

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I can't believe you don't like baked beans. Beans on toast is a classic.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: It is, but no, not for me. Let's quickly recap the vocabulary we learnt during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We learnt often, which means we do something a lot, and we learnt how often, which we use to ask someone how many times they do something.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Usually, normally and generally, which are all ways to talk about things we do a lot.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Sometimes, which we can use to talk about things we do, but not always or often.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And never. To talk about things we don't do, like eat beans, Beth.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes, just like I never eat baked beans. Horrible.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Thanks for listening to Real Easy English. Visit our website for more activities and courses to help you with your English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Next week, we'll talk about our friends.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: See you then. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Thank you.
